name: Gabapentinoids
summary: Gabapentinoids are the group that contains pregabalin and gabapentin, which are used for epilepsy and nerve pain.
mechanism: For epilepsy, these medicines are thought to reduce abnormal electrical activity in the brain. For nerve pain, they are thought to block pain by affecting pain messages travelling through the brain and down the spine.
cautions: The NHS lists drowsiness and dizziness among the common side effects of both medicines.
The NHS says some people can become addicted to either medicine.
The NHS says that when stopping either medicine the dose is reduced gradually to avoid withdrawal symptoms.

classInteractions.with: Opioids, alcohol and other medicines that cause sleepiness
classInteractions.effect: The MHRA says gabapentin and pregabalin can cause potentially fatal respiratory depression, particularly when used with opioid medicines and alcohol.

source.title: MHRA Drug Safety Update: Pregabalin (Lyrica), gabapentin (Neurontin) and risk of abuse and dependence

classWarnings.text: Pregabalin and gabapentin became Class C controlled drugs, and Schedule 3 under the Misuse of Drugs Regulations 2001, on 1 April 2019.

source.title: GOV.UK: Reclassification of pregabalin and gabapentin to Schedule 3 drugs from 1 April 2019

classWarnings.text: The MHRA reports severe breathing difficulty with pregabalin, and a separate update covers gabapentin.

source.title: MHRA Drug Safety Update: Pregabalin (Lyrica) reports of severe respiratory depression
